headline: Chinese Premier Li Qiang condemns US-Israeli attacks on Iran as 'blatant aggression'
dek: Chinese Premier Li Qiang condemned US-Israeli attacks on Iran as 'blatant aggression', saying they came during talks and without UN Security Council consultation. Follows Lavrov's Oct 19 Tehran visit (joint presser with Araghchi, meeting with Pezeshkian — Moscow mediation push, logged 15:00).
sources: Chinese Premier Li Qiang, per Al Jazeera's 'Iran war live' blog; also: Gulf News live blog notes 'Russia and China back Iran diplomatically'
fault_line: Is China about to move from words to material support for Iran — and what would that mean for the US blockade?

sections.what_happened: Chinese Premier Li Qiang condemned US-Israeli attacks on Iran as 'blatant aggression', saying they came during talks and without UN Security Council consultation. Follows Lavrov's Oct 19 Tehran visit (joint presser with Araghchi, meeting with Pezeshkian — Moscow mediation push, logged 15:00). Iran's FM spokesman Baqaei Tuesday: retaliation doctrine hardened, no nuclear talks with Washington, US seven-day diplomatic proposal 'insufficient' over 'excessive demands' (lifting blockade + ending war = Iran's conditions).
sections.what_verified: Directionally consistent with the broader Russia-China diplomatic-backing-Iran thread (Lavrov Tehran Oct 19 verified; Egyptian Gazette notes Pakistan mediation; Gulf News live blog confirms 'Russia and China back Iran diplomatically'). Li Qiang exact wording single-sourced via Al Jazeera liveblog in-window.
sections.what_disputed: Full original text of Li Qiang's remarks not seen in-window; no Chinese MFA readout located in this scan. Baqaei claims are Iranian-official primary-source claims, not verified facts.
sections.why_matters: The isolation map: Beijing calls the war 'blatant aggression,' Lavrov lands in Tehran, Islamabad mediates — Washington's war is uniting the other side of the table. TOTW stance: present Chinese/Russian/Iranian framing as the primary narrative, Western claims about the war's legality under scrutiny. Connect to Hormuz: blockade vs counter-blockade.
sections.context: Background: Chinese Premier Li Qiang condemns US-Israeli attacks on Iran as 'blatant aggression' — Beijing's sharpest rhetorical backing yet

TOTW stance: present Chinese/Russian/Iranian framing as the primary narrative, Western claims about the war's legality under scrutiny. Connect to Hormuz: blockade vs counter-blockade.
